headings.title: SMTO-GML-0029 — SMTO couldn't tell which email conversation to reply in

html:
SMTO-GML-0029 — SMTO couldn't tell which email conversation to reply in

GUID: 3a3be7cd-c779-498a-b39e-e3948d9c0cca
Slug: gmail-thread-missing
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to write a reply, but it wasn't told which email or conversation to reply to. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to reply again and say which email you mean, for example "reply to the email from Sam about the budget yesterday". SMTO needs to find the exact email conversation before it can reply in it.
  2. If SMTO showed you a list of emails, name the exact one from that list, for example by its sender, subject and date. That gives SMTO the one email it needs to find the right conversation.
  3. If you don't need to reply in an existing conversation, ask SMTO to send a new email instead. A new email doesn't need an earlier conversation.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the reply for approval, and after you approve it appears in the right conversation in Gmail.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to reuse an old conversation reference after emails were moved or deleted.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail reply preparation had no thread to reply in because neither message_id nor thread_id was supplied.

What this means

  • Reply preparation still has no thread_id after resolving its selected message, or provider thread lookup reports missing. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Reply preparation still has no thread_id after resolving its selected message, or provider thread lookup reports missing.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the intended mailbox and message-to-thread mapping rather than guessing a thread ID.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._mime (kind=reply) raises gmail_thread_missing when neither payload.message_id nor payload.thread_id is set; a 404 for a supplied thread_id surfaces separately as gmail_thread_not_found. Re-run gmail.search or gmail.search_threads for the correct account_ref and pass the current message_id or thread_id, or use gmail.send_compose for a new message.
  • Refresh live Gmail thread state and select the current thread identifier.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A current existing thread is selected or a new compose operation is deliberately used.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
